analysis:
Both units are head-side excerpts of CHANGELOG.md (lines 601-1054). They carry no patch hunks, no base text and no source code, so I could not tell which lines changed. This is a documentation-only view and a coverage limit, not evidence that the underlying code is safe.

The changelog describes security-relevant behavior that the next pass should check against the actual code diffs:
- App Attest serving authorization (TB-011, T-052..T-058, A-015..A-017): protocol-3-only serving, CDhash extensions accepted without the ED flag (~606, 610), CandidateCDHash unique-binding to the full 32-byte CodeDirectory hash (612), durable build qualification and revocation (647-648, 686), and final-handoff fencing (696). Check that each gate fails closed.
- Retry and recovery logic (613-615, 627-628, 680): retries must not extend leases or authorize without a fresh assertion and a verified risk receipt.
- Legacy trust path (TB-009, T-036): the legacy self_signed, hardware, MDA and APNs fields must stay unchanged and independent of App Attest.
- Public attestation roster privacy (609, TB-009): private-only providers are excluded before shared caching. Public SE keys still link sessions.
- Payments (TB-008, ~951-956): a new Stripe Global Payouts route is described as enabled by default in the next production release. TB-008 should be updated to cover payout atomicity and idempotency, the ambiguous-payout manual-review handling, and webhook reconciliation (T-030, A-009).
- Promotions and token grants (~701-711): atomic caps, reservation and settlement, and sponsored provider earnings affect the ledger (A-009).
- Other items to confirm in code: the account-scoped first-content SLA env gate, the Responses `instructions` change, and the strict negative-token-budget validation.

No concrete regression can be shown from changelog text alone. The integration pass should confirm TB-008 and T-030 coverage of the Global Payouts route once the implementing code is visible.
